newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Battle for Mogadishu widens, 135 dead, 900 wounded.
newsitem.headline: Battle for Mogadishu widens, 135 dead, 900 wounded.

text.p: The battle for the Somali capital Mogadishu widened on Tuesday when another major faction joined the fighting, which has killed more than 135 people and wounded 900 in five days.
Witnesses said militiamen under north Mogadishu alliance chief Ali Mahdi Mohamed shelled Hussein Aideed's south Mogadishu "presidential" palace and other positions held by his forces.
Ali Mahdi's four-wheel-drive battlewagons fired cannon at the K-4 junction in south Mogadishu, the capital's closed airport and residential areas.

Hussein Aideed's gunners fired a few mortar bombs into north Mogadishu in retaliation. Two rounds slammed into Manapolio district, killing two people and wounding seven. A third hit ruins of a hotel wrecked earlier in the civil war.
It was the first time Ali Mahdi's forces had joined the fighting in earnest. The latest round of violence erupted last Friday and has killed more than 135 people, according to hospital sources.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said in a statement some 900 wounded were admitted to seven hospitals and medical centres in the city since Friday and more than 70 people had died of their wounds while undergoing treatment.
The ICRC said the compound at south Mogadishu's Digfer hospital, the largest in the south, was hit by a shell on Sunday, apparently prompting people to stay away in fear of another attack.

"We are appalled by the apparently high number of civilian casualties, which are a result of indiscriminate firing into places like markets where ordinary people gather," said Fred Grimm, head of ICRC Somalia.
"We understand thousands of people have left their homes to seek safety. Many of them have left Medina district in particular. If this continues public health problems could arise," he said.
Hospital sources said 12 people were killed and more than 25 wounded in southern Mogadishu on Tuesday, including three women who were killed when a mortar bomb crashed into their house.

Another nine were killed and 16 wounded when fierce fighting erupted on Tuesday evening in the Hosh area in Medina district, hospital sources said. A mortar blast near Bakara market wounded three people.

"We'll stop shelling when Hussein Aideed ends his aggression on civilians in Medina," said Ali Mahdi's spokesman Hussein Sheikh Ahmed Kadare. The bombardment of Medina could no longer be tolerated, he said.
Medina's population consists mostly of members of the same Abgal sub-clan as Ali Mahdi, the Aideed family's arch-enemy.
Kadare said all-out war was almost inevitable in the city.

Before Ali Mahdi's faction entered the fray, street battles had centred on southern Mogadishu, pitting Aideed's forces against gunmen loyal to rival leaders Osman Hassan Ali Atto and Musa Sudi Yalahow, the Moslem fundamentalist chief of Medina district.
Sporadic shooting could be heard in Medina on Tuesday.
Fighting at the airport with mortars and heavy weapons began when Aideed's forces thrust towards the southern end of the runway which is held by Yalahow's forces, allied with Ali Mahdi.
Aideed's radio station in south Mogadishu said on Sunday night the national army was "cleansing bandits" from Medina.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August and was elected president of Somalia by his own supporters. But both he and his government are rejected by most other faction leaders.

The airport has been closed to all flights since the last U.N. peacekeepers pulled out of Somalia in March 1995. Even if one faction controlled the whole airport area, it would have to remain closed because it is in range of other factions' guns.
